# RP-AXE Band-1 Tree Review

## 1. Verdict
Band-1 is **balanced and plausible**. Tier pacing is an even content-node diamond, the critical path to orbit is a clean 9-node, every-step-+1-tier climb that peaks at a T4 orbital engine, and the parallel kerolox/Soviet/storable/hydrolox lines read as differentiated peers rather than a hierarchy. Curation is strong across all 18 lanes (the "id lies, title tells truth" discipline is clearly applied — every classic id-trap resolved correctly, zero untriaged hubs, all tier jumps justified); the surviving issues are one real discipline-instantiation bug (CompositeMaterials debuts on an aluminum upgrade), one mis-homed engine ride-along, a couple of catalog/naming slips, and two uncertain judgment calls — none of which threaten the overall balance or plausibility.

## 2. Balance

**Tier pacing — clean diamond.** Judged by *content* (non-catalog) nodes, the per-tier census is T1:13, T2:16, T3:15, T4:15, T5:5, T6:0, T7:0 — no starved or bloated content tier, 2.8–4.4 content-parts/node (well under the ≤6 cap). Raw part totals (84/145/149/127/38 for T1–T5) are a poor balance signal: ~2/3 of the ~619 parts sit in exempt catalog/utility nodes (the MLP inventory alone is ~231 parts), so the T2–T4 raw bulge is intentional catalog mass, not content bloat. T6/T7 hold *zero* content nodes — each is a single GroundSupport MLP reference shelf (Saturn T6, Shuttle T7), so the playable tree is T1–T5 by design. Every parent→child edge is forward; exactly 8 edges span ≥2 tiers and all 8 are justified or on the intentional list (aero_subsonicWing T1→supersonic T3; X-2→X-15 T3→T5; film-return→film-recon T1→T3; hydrolox T2→T4; the three crossover AND-gates tier-pinned to gap-1 by their elec_transistor co-parent; nuc_geiger T1→cosmic-ray T3 vacuum-tube coincidence).

**Critical path to orbit — well-paced.** 9 nodes beyond `start`, orbit engine at T4, every step +1 tier: engine spine `start`→pc_storables(T1)→fd_turbopumpFeed(T2)→fd_verniers(T3)→fd_orbitalSoviet R-7(T4) [the Atlas fd_largeChamber path is identical length] + tank met_weldedTank(T1) + structure str_structuralHardware(T1)→str_staging(T2) + guidance gnc_postWarAvionics(T1)→gnc_avionicsPrototypes(T2). A 4-generation engine climb (turbopump→trim→cluster) dominates the path and lands orbit ~80% up the playable T1–T5 range as the band's climax. A scrappier small-sat orbit (Vanguard single-chamber T3 / Explorer turbopump+composite-solid kick) is reachable one tier earlier — a good historical spread, not an imbalance.

**Gates — no do-nothing convergences.** Zero forbidden empty many→one gates. `cryo_hydrogen` (T1, 1 parent) is the one allowed empty commitment gate; `elec_transistor` (T3) is also empty but is a single-parent→5-child enabler (the blessed "solid-state gate"), the opposite topology; `fd_turbopumpFeed`'s anyToUnlock (2 parents) is a real parts node. Hub census is healthy — only `start` (15, exempt root), `elec_transistor` (5, accepted), and `str_structuralHardware` (4, accepted) exceed the >3-dependent threshold, and the 7 multi-parent convergences are all deliberate two-lane crossovers carrying real parts/grants.

**Parallel-path peer balance — peers, not a hierarchy.**
- *Hydrolox gamble holds:* RZ.20 (410 Isp/70 kN, T2) → RL-10 (422 Isp/66 kN, T4) out-Isps every kerolox (which tops out at RD-119 362, T5), but 70 kN confines it to upper stages, so it can't dominate (needs the kerolox spine beneath it) and won't wither (high-energy-upper niche) — complementary, and well-tiered (RL-10 T4 precedes kerolox-vacuum RD-0110 T5).
- *T4 three-way fork:* Soviet R-7 cluster (RD-107/108, 312–320 Isp + integral verniers) ‖ storable multichamber (YF-2/RD-211, 253–267 Isp, storable propellant, up to 1214 kN) are cleanly differentiated peers. The **Western single-chamber** (fd_largeChamber: LR79/RZ/LR89, 288–305 Isp) is the squeezed one — Isp-dominated by the Soviet line and needing a bolt-on fd_verniers node the Soviet cluster gets for free — rescued only at the *path* level by the high-Isp LR105 Atlas sustainer sitting one tier up. This is flagged as an intentional parallel-path design and is a cost/balance lever explicitly **deferred / out of scope** for this pass, not a broken rule.
- *Isp-ladder annotation* (nodes.yaml line 146) is right for solids (199–239) and storables/HTP/hypergolic (220–272) but slightly overstates early kerolox: the ethanol/LOX spine *root* is ~235–265, interleaving the storable band; kerolox earns 290–320 only at T3–T4 after the RP-1 switch. Tiers capture the climb; the flat one-line comment label does not (immaterial, comment prose only).
- *Aviation is a true optional side-quest:* verified that **no** orbit-path node depends on any jet / rocketplane / supersonic-wing / landing-gear node. The only shared aero is aero_subsonicWing (the aero root: control surfaces + intakes, used by fairings/recovery), not aviation-specific.

## 3. Plausibility findings (confirmed)
Grouped by lane, highest confidence first; uncertain items marked.

### CompositeMaterials
- **`cmp_compositeFairings`** — The band-1 debut node for the entire CompositeMaterials discipline is titled "Composite Fairing Shells" (T4) with flavor "resin-bonded fibre instead of spun metal," but it delivers only `PFTech-Fairing-I`, whose real RP-1 title is **"Aluminum Fairings and Stringers"** (rung I of a 6-rung ladder: I Aluminum → II Magnesium → III Fiberglass → IV Isogrid → **V Composite** → VI Advanced Composite; composite = `PFTech-Fairing-V`, gated at materialsScienceLongTerm, far beyond band 1). So the discipline whose whole identity is *composites* rests on a node that actually contains aluminum — title, flavor, and discipline all over-claim the delivered rung. → **Fix:** rename/re-flavor the band-1 node to its true rung-I content (e.g. "Aluminum Fairing Shells" / a generic "lighter fairing shells") and either re-home it into the metal-materials lane (Metallurgy/Aerodynamics) or defer the CompositeMaterials discipline debut to the actual composite rung V in a later band; at minimum stop the flavor claiming "fibre instead of spun metal" when it ships spun-metal aluminum. — **[High]** *(sourced from the CompositeMaterials lane assessment; ground-truthed against PFTechLevels.cfg + upgrades-curated.tsv for this report.)*

(Correct failure mode is mis-homed ride-along, not id-lie — id and title are both "XLR41".) — **[High]** *(reviewer marked low, but verify found the part data unambiguous.)*

## Gap-close addendum (2026-07-03)

The 4 agents that failed the structured-output step in the main pass, plus the degenerate Aerodynamics lane, were re-run. **Net result: 0 new confirmed findings** — every recovered lane corroborates the "balanced and plausible" verdict.

- **Metallurgy** — *model lane, near-zero drift.* welded->stainless->nimonic materials line + welded->isogrid tank branch all read true; tanks cleanly partitioned by structure-mode/tier (conventional->isogrid->balloon), no cross-lane leakage; rule-#4 engine-upgrade homing textbook (thrust-uprates on stainless, the rockets*jets crossover on nimonic). 2 nits **refuted** (`met_isogrid->th_hermeticBus` reroot would create a tier fault; lone `ca_tank_mp_s` tank is on-theme, not a catalog shelf).
- **AirBreathing** — *solid, coherent.* piston->centrifugal->axial->{afterburner || variable-stator}->ramjet is a true generational succession; the `aero_supersonicWing` shock-cone crossover gates both supersonic-jet nodes correctly. 1 nit **refuted** (`prop_recipEngine` 9-part piston root = standard same-family foundation catalog).
- **Microelectronics** — *small, mostly clean.* every id ground-truthed; `elec_transistor` is the accepted 5-way solid-state hub; instrument AND-gates sound. 2 low-confidence `mic_atmoSounding` nits (mission-style name; weak magnetometer heritage edge) — verify inconclusive (agents died) but reviewer self-marked likely-intentional and the main run already reasoned them through as the intended discipline anchor. **Not actionable.**
- **Aerodynamics** — *balanced, coherent* (re-run as a plain-text agent after two schema-forcing failures). subsonic root (control + intakes) -> {recovery || supersonic swept-wing+shock-cone || boattail->fairings->{composite || prefab-nose}}; both catalog dead-ends (stamped wings, prefab nose cones) correctly opt-in and on the intentional list. 6 candidates all **refuted** (hub count 3 < accepted 5; recovery edge is same-family bluff-body decel; fairings naming is the device-class mechanism; airbrake at home in supersonic; parts-counts not a rubric mode; `boattail->stamped-wings` is the labeled gating tax).
- **tier-audit sweep** — 91 edges, gap distribution `{1:83, 2:6, 3:2}`, zero non-forward; all 8 multi-tier jumps on the intentional list; **0 unjustified**.

*(Two verify agents for the Microelectronics nits also hit the schema-forcing failure; those two items are low-confidence and likely-intentional, so verification-inconclusive is immaterial to the verdict.)*
